subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job and heartbeat provenance-backed elevated exec authority, and how should existing wildcard cron-event or heartbeat elevated configurations upgrade?
rationale: The issue affects privileged host execution and persistent scheduler state; automation cannot safely choose between preserving wildcard compatibility, adding strict provenance, or failing closed for existing users.

options.title: Design provenance-backed grants
options.body: Add non-forgeable approved creator/updater/execution provenance for cron and heartbeat elevation, plus migration or doctor repair for wildcard configurations.

options.title: Fold into scheduler RFC
options.body: Make this the elevated-exec slice of the broader scheduling provenance design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71712, explicitly covering heartbeat too.

options.title: Keep current allowFrom model
options.body: Document internal-source wildcard elevation as operator-owned trusted configuration and close only after maintainers decide the risk is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Design provenance-backed grants
recommendation.body: Add non-forgeable approved creator/updater/execution provenance for cron and heartbeat elevation, plus migration or doctor repair for wildcard configurations.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest recent cron security-boundary implementation and have the strongest concrete history on the affected scheduler path.
